title: Motor accident compensation is a statutory welfare-oriented regime under the Motor Vehicles Act 1988

content.overview: Motor accident compensation is a statutory welfare-oriented regime under the Motor Vehicles Act 1988. MACT proceedings focus on just compensation, statutory liability and structured assessment of dependency, disability and other heads.
content.glance: Motor accident compensation is a statutory welfare-oriented regime under the Motor Vehicles Act 1988. MACT proceedings focus on just compensation, statutory liability and structured assessment of dependency, disability and other heads.
content.study: Motor accident compensation is a statutory welfare-oriented regime under the Motor Vehicles Act 1988. MACT proceedings focus on just compensation, statutory liability and structured assessment of dependency, disability and other heads.\n\nThe Motor Vehicles Act creates a specialised compensation system distinct from ordinary tort litigation. Sarla Verma standardised multiplier methodology; Pranay Sethi addressed future prospects and conventional heads. Later decisions continue to refine these principles.

sections.heading: Provenance, Legislative Objective & Doctrinal Foundations
sections.body: The Motor Vehicles Act creates a specialised compensation system distinct from ordinary tort litigation. Sarla Verma standardised multiplier methodology; Pranay Sethi addressed future prospects and conventional heads. Later decisions continue to refine these principles.

sections.heading: Textual Anatomy, Provisos & Statutory Deconstruction
sections.body: Relevant provisions are in Chapters XI and XII of the Motor Vehicles Act, subject to amendments and current statutory text. Different statutory routes have different proof requirements.

sections.heading: Mandatory Proving Ingredients & Essential Elements
sections.body: 1. Covered motor accident. 2. Statutory claimant standing. 3. Death or bodily injury or qualifying loss. 4. Negligence where required by the route. 5. Proof of income, age, dependants and disability. 6. Apply statutory compensation methodology.

sections.heading: Evidentiary Burdens under BSA 2023 (ss. 104–106 & s. 63)
sections.body: Medical records, FIR, site plan, post-mortem report, income proof, disability certificate and dependency evidence are central. MACT proceedings are civil in character.

sections.heading: Procedural Roadmap, Competent Forum & Limitation Act Checkpoints
sections.body: Claims are brought before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal having statutory jurisdiction. Appeals lie under the Act. Check current limitation and procedural provisions.
